# slate 0.1.0 command line

Every command accepts `--json` and then prints exactly one JSON object on stdout with `slate`, `format`, `command`, `ok`, `errors`, `warnings` and `diagnostics` fields plus the command's own fields. Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` errors or failed checks, `2` bad command line.

| command | what it does |
|---|---|
| [`slate new PATH [FLAGS]`](#slate-new) | Create a project from the starter template |
| [`slate check [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#slate-check) | Validate every project file without running anything |
| [`slate run [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#slate-run) | Run a scene headless for N frames |
| [`slate shot [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#slate-shot) | Render a frame to PNG, with a text report of what is drawn where |
| [`slate inspect [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#slate-inspect) | Dump the world state at a frame as JSON (or a table) |
| [`slate test [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#slate-test) | Run playtests: scripted input, expectations and reference screenshots |
| [`slate explain [TOPIC] [FLAGS]`](#slate-explain) | Explain a diagnostic code, a file format/component, or a command |
| [`slate schema [KIND] [FLAGS]`](#slate-schema) | Print the JSON Schema of a file format |
| [`slate docs [FLAGS]`](#slate-docs) | Print the reference docs for this exact slate version |
| [`slate serve [PATH] [FLAGS]`](#slate-serve) | Serve the web player for a project (reloads when files change) |
| [`slate help [COMMAND] [FLAGS]`](#slate-help) | Show help for slate or a command |
| [`slate version [FLAGS]`](#slate-version) | Print the slate version |

## slate new

```text
slate new — Create a project from the starter template

Usage: slate new PATH [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  PATH         Folder to create (must not exist or be empty).

Flags:
  --name NAME        Project name (default: the folder name).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Writes slate.toml, a starter scene, prefabs, a playtest and an AGENTS.md generated for this slate version, then checks the result.

Examples:
  slate new my-game
  slate new games/maze --name "Maze"
```

## slate check

```text
slate check — Validate every project file without running anything

Usage: slate check [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to slate.toml.

Flags:
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Parses slate.toml, every scene, prefab and playtest; checks types, unknown keys, references between files and static problems (overlapping solids, signals that can never fire). Exit code 1 if there are errors; warnings do not fail.

Examples:
  slate check
  slate check my-game --json
```

## slate run

```text
slate run — Run a scene headless for N frames

Usage: slate run [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to slate.toml.

Flags:
  --frames N         Frames (fixed steps) to run. Default: the playtest's frames, else 300.
  --input FILE       Drive the scene with a playtest's [[input]] (and use its scene and seed).
  --seed N           Override the random seed.
  --events           Include the event log.
  --hash-every N     Record the state hash every N frames (to find where two runs diverge).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Deterministic: the same files, input and seed always give the same state hash, on every platform. No window and no GPU are used.

Examples:
  slate run --frames 300
  slate run tests/walkthrough.toml --events
  slate run scenes/garden.toml --input tests/walkthrough.toml --json
```

## slate shot

```text
slate shot — Render a frame to PNG, with a text report of what is drawn where

Usage: slate shot [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to slate.toml.

Flags:
  --frame N          Frame to render. Default: the playtest's last frame, else 0.
  --input FILE       Drive the scene with a playtest's [[input]] (and use its scene and seed).
  --seed N           Override the random seed.
  --out FILE         PNG path. Default: out/<scene>_f<frame>.png in the project.
  --compare FILE     Compare with a reference PNG; exit 1 if it differs (writes <out>.diff.png).
  --max-diff N       With --compare: pixels allowed to differ (default 0).
  --report           Print the frame report (always included with --json).
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Rendering is a deterministic CPU rasterizer: identical pixels on every machine. The frame report lists each entity's screen rectangle, visible pixels and what covers it, and flags off-screen (W0301), hidden (W0302) and clipped (W0303) entities.

Examples:
  slate shot
  slate shot --input tests/walkthrough.toml --report
  slate shot --frame 120 --out a.png --json
```

## slate inspect

```text
slate inspect — Dump the world state at a frame as JSON (or a table)

Usage: slate inspect [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to slate.toml.

Flags:
  --frame N          Frame to inspect. Default: the playtest's last frame, else 0.
  --input FILE       Drive the scene with a playtest's [[input]] (and use its scene and seed).
  --seed N           Override the random seed.
  --entity NAME      Only this entity (and, with --events, its events).
  --component NAME   Only entities with this component (sprite, trigger, ...).
  --events           Include the event log: what happened and what was refused, and why.
  --since N          With --events: only events from frame N on.
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Answers what exists, where it is, and why something happened. Entities include every component, runtime state (cooldowns, patrol targets, trigger occupants) and their screen rectangle.

Examples:
  slate inspect --json
  slate inspect --input tests/walkthrough.toml --frame 60 --entity player --events
```

## slate test

```text
slate test — Run playtests: scripted input, expectations and reference screenshots

Usage: slate test [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder or a single playtest file (default: current folder).

Flags:
  --filter TEXT      Only playtests whose name contains TEXT.
  --update-refs      Write reference images from the current output instead of comparing.
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Runs every tests/*.toml. Failed expectations are E0401 with the entity's recent events; image mismatches are E0402 and write the actual and diff images under out/tests/.

Examples:
  slate test
  slate test --filter walk --json
  slate test --update-refs
```

## slate explain

```text
slate explain — Explain a diagnostic code, a file format/component, or a command

Usage: slate explain [TOPIC] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [TOPIC]      A code (E0103), a component or format (sprite, entity, connect, playtest) or a command. Omit to list topics.

Flags:
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Like `rustc --explain`, for slate's codes and file formats.

Examples:
  slate explain
  slate explain E0201
  slate explain sprite
  slate explain trigger --json
```

## slate schema

```text
slate schema — Print the JSON Schema of a file format

Usage: slate schema [KIND] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [KIND]       project, scene, prefab or playtest. Omit to list them.

Flags:
  --out DIR          Write all schemas into DIR as <kind>.schema.json.
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Editors (e.g. VS Code + Even Better TOML) can use these for completion and inline errors.

Examples:
  slate schema scene
  slate schema --out .slate/schema
```

## slate docs

```text
slate docs — Print the reference docs for this exact slate version

Usage: slate docs [FLAGS]

Flags:
  --agents           Print the AGENTS.md that `slate new` writes into projects.
  --out DIR          Write cli.md, formats.md, errors.md and schemas/ into DIR.
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

Docs are generated from the same registries the engine uses, so they always match the installed version.

Examples:
  slate docs
  slate docs --agents > AGENTS.md
```

## slate serve

```text
slate serve — Serve the web player for a project (reloads when files change)

Usage: slate serve [PATH] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [PATH]       Project folder, scene file or playtest file (default: current folder). The project is found by walking up to slate.toml.

Flags:
  --port N           Port on 127.0.0.1 (default 4410).
  --wasm FILE        Path to slate_web.wasm (default: the workspace build, see `cargo xtask web`).

Opens nothing by itself; visit the printed URL. URL parameters: scene=PATH, input=PATH, frames=N (run N frames immediately, then pause). The page shows the frame number and state hash, which match `slate run` for the same input.

Examples:
  slate serve examples/iso_garden
  slate serve --port 8080
```

## slate help

```text
slate help — Show help for slate or a command

Usage: slate help [COMMAND] [FLAGS]

Arguments:
  [COMMAND]    Command to describe.

Flags:
  --json             Print one JSON object on stdout instead of text.

`slate help --json` lists every command, argument and flag as data.

Examples:
  slate help
  slate help shot
  slate help --json
```
